name: kitchensink4xl
description: Everything plus the kitchen sink for Microsoft Excel: the .xlsx MCP server that never hands your AI a number it cannot back up.
long_description: A Model Context Protocol server for Microsoft Excel workbooks. 129 distinct operations across 67 tools, covering cells and ranges, an anchored grid view, server-side query and aggregation, formula writing and auditing, structural row and column edits that carry formulas, tables, named ranges, charts and cross-sheet references with them, Excel-exact sorting and filtering, formatting and named styles, conditional formatting, data validation, images and charts, page layout, comments and hyperlinks, import and export, inspectors, backups and diagnostics. A spreadsheet stores its answers, not its thinking, so every value a read returns is labeled calculated, cached, or absent, and a read that touches stale cells names them by address. Tools load in tiers: a 40 tool lite core opens the session at about 14,500 tokens, and packs are enabled on demand. The file tier needs no Excel installed and runs anywhere. The optional COM pack drives a private hidden Excel instance for real recalculation, real pivot tables, goal seek, PDF export and format conversion; it requires Windows with Microsoft Excel installed and never touches the workbook you have open on screen. Launching this bundle requires uv (the uvx command) on your machine; the server itself is fetched from PyPI on first launch. Tip: in Claude Desktop's Tool permissions, set the Read-only tools group to Always Allow: those tools cannot change anything, and it stops most permission prompts.

verify_with_excel.title: Verify every save with Excel
verify_with_excel.description: After every save, open the result in a hidden copy of Excel and restore the backup if Excel would show a repair prompt. The strictest safety setting there is. It costs a round trip through Excel on every write, so it is off by default, and it needs Windows with Excel installed. Individual tool calls can still ask for it one save at a time with verify_com.

allowed_root.title: Limit the server to one folder (optional)
allowed_root.description: Leave this empty and the server reads and writes wherever you point it, which is the normal setup. Set it to a folder and every path the server touches, reads included, has to be inside that folder or the call refuses before any file is opened. Worth setting when an agent works unattended.
